chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Sammal, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Hakim ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Hafs al-A'war asked him, saying: 'Indeed the Sultanate buys from us the water-skins and the containers, and they appoint an agent until he takes the full amount from us, so we bribe him so that he does not wrong us.' He said: 'There is no harm in what you use to rectify your wealth.' Then he was silent for a moment, then he said: 'Do you see if you bribe him and he takes less than the condition (of the bribe/agreed amount)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then your bribe is invalid (corrupted).'

key_terms.اَلْأَعْوَر: The one-eyed (a title/nickname for the narrator Hafs)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bribing government officials to prevent injustice in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between permissible bribery to prevent injustice (*li-taslih al-mal*) and invalid bribery based on the official's acceptance of less than the agreed sum. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of the transaction depends on the specific conditions and the integrity of the exchange, rather than a blanket prohibition. The hadith serves as a practical legal precedent for navigating administrative corruption while maintaining religious compliance.
